root_cause.text: An off-by-one bounds check in stm32_usbphyc_probe() allowed a device-tree "reg" index equal to usbphyc->nphys to be accepted and then used to access usbphyc->phys[] past the end of the array.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (ret || index > usbphyc->nphys)` to `if (ret || index >= usbphyc->nphys)`, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that `usbphyc->phys[]` has `usbphyc->nphys` elements so `index == usbphyc->nphys` is "one element out of bounds."

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject `reg` values equal to the PHY count in `stm32_usbphyc_probe()` to fix an off-by-one bounds check.
intent_record.what: The conditional check after reading the child node's "reg" property was changed from `index > usbphyc->nphys` to `index >= usbphyc->nphys` in `stm32_usbphyc_probe()`.
intent_record.how: This makes the bounds check reject an index equal to `usbphyc->nphys`, preventing an out-of-range PHY index from being treated as valid and avoiding potential invalid array access or misconfiguration during probe.

grouping_result.intent: Reject `reg` values equal to the PHY count in `stm32_usbphyc_probe()` to fix an off-by-one bounds check.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the described off-by-one bug by rejecting a device-tree `reg` index equal to `usbphyc->nphys` in `stm32_usbphyc_probe()`, preventing out-of-bounds access to `usbphyc->phys[]`.

candidates.rationale: This bounds check is off by one: it rejects indices greater than nphys, but incorrectly accepts index == nphys. That permits an out-of-bounds access to usbphyc->phys[index].

vuln_statements.explanation: This bounds check is off by one: it only rejects indices greater than usbphyc->nphys, but incorrectly allows index == usbphyc->nphys. That accepted value can then be used to access usbphyc->phys[] one past the end of the array, causing the out-of-bounds condition described in the root cause.

commit 94c358da3a0545205c6c6a50ae26141f1c73acfa
Author: Amelie Delaunay <amelie.delaunay@st.com>
Date:   Fri Mar 2 15:56:25 2018 +0100

    phy: stm32: add support for STM32 USB PHY Controller (USBPHYC)
    
    This patch adds phy transceiver driver for STM32 USB PHY Controller
    (USBPHYC) that provides dual port High-Speed phy for OTG (single port)
    and EHCI/OHCI host controller (two ports).
    One port of the phy is shared between the two USB controllers through
    a UTMI+ switch.
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is visible in stm32_usbphyc_probe(). The code reads the child DT "reg" value with `ret = of_property_read_u32(child, "reg", &index);` and validates it using `if (ret || index > usbphyc->nphys)`. This is the off-by-one check described in the root cause: a value equal to `usbphyc->nphys` is accepted because only `>` is rejected. Since valid array indices for `usbphyc->phys` are `0 .. usbphyc->nphys - 1`, allowing `index == usbphyc->nphys` is incorrect. The fix would require rejecting `index >= usbphyc->nphys`, but that is not present here. The function then stores and later uses this accepted index via `usbphyc->phys[port]->index = index;`, so the bad DT value can propagate and be used as a physical port index, matching the reported root cause. Therefore this commit contains the vulnerable construct and does not yet contain the fix.
